source.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Connor Kissane; Robert Krzyzanowski; J. Bloom; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Specialisation and polysemanticity of induction heads; token-specific feature decomposition

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures induction behavior and investigates induction-related features and heads using SAE feature analysis, induction scores, and prompt corruption rather than reproducing the original training-time measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior induction-head findings and reports many SAE evaluation results unrelated to the claim. Those are not recorded as rows. The reported GPT-2 loss-ablation comparison for head 10.2 concerns digit copying and URL completion, not induction behavior.
record.test_reason: The study does not train models. It uses SAE feature attribution, ablation, induction scores and prompt corruption to show induction heads and induction-by-copying features in trained GELU-2L and GPT-2 Small. These results bear on the presence of induction behaviour across models (V4) and on the [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying mechanism (V1). It does not test previous-token composition or training dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that attention-output SAEs reveal induction feature families. The SAEs also motivated the hypothesis, then confirmed without SAEs, that GPT-2 Small's heads 5.1 and 5.5 specialise in long- vs short-prefix induction. They present this as partly explaining seemingly redundant induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE feature interpretation and attribution, induction-score measurements, and prompt corruption; it does not reproduce the original training-time phase-change and in-context-learning loss measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefix length changes the induction scores of GPT-2 Small heads 5.1 and 5.5; corrupting a long-prefix example changes the heads’ measured induction scores differently.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, induction heads differ in specialisation. Head 5.1's induction score is <0.3 for 1-token prefixes and rises above 0.7 for long prefixes. Head 5.5 already does 1-prefix induction at about 0.7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multiple induction heads in one model are not redundant; they specialise by prefix length (long-prefix vs short-prefix induction).

record.problems: The authors describe the automated feature-selection and behavior heuristics as crude and potentially prone to false positives and false negatives. Several interpretations rely on qualitative analysis. The induction-head experiments do not measure training-time formation or in-context-learning dynamics.

untested.parts: Formation through K-composition with an earlier previous-token head; attention-only models; formation during training.
Entire version: no in-context-learning loss by token index and no share of in-context learning attributed to induction heads.
Training runs, other architectures and modalities. Gemma-2B is covered only by a qualitative statement.
Entire version: prefix-length specialisation is not about formation transitions.

missing.what: States that induction features occur in all models studied, including Gemma-2B; qualitative, no numbers.
Direct logit attribution vs prefix length (5.1 rises sharply, 5.5 flat); on real training-data samples, 5.1 mostly does long-prefix and 5.5 mostly 1-prefix induction.
Head survey identifies further induction heads in GPT-2 Small (6.9, 7.10; non-standard 7.2, 10.10) and a previous-token head 4.11.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily an SAE methods paper. GELU-2L has MLP layers, so the V1 links rest on the copying mechanism in a small 2-layer model, not on an attention-only replication. No original-source overlap.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test formation through composition with an earlier previous-token head in a small attention-only transformer, or induction-head formation during training.
The study does not measure induction-head formation over training time, in-context-learning loss changes over token index, or a training-loss bump.
The study does not measure how much in-context learning in large transformers is carried by induction heads.

Evidence is limited to induction behavior in GELU-2L and GPT-2 Small. It does not establish universality across training runs, other architectures, or modalities; Gemma-2B is included in SAE evaluations, but no specific induction-head result is reported for it.
The study does not compare training data or training setups for their effects on induction-head formation or persistent in-context learning.
The study does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.
The study distinguishes short- and long-prefix induction behavior, not separate formation transitions during training.

rows.subject: GELU-2L
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the board-induction SAE feature and measured the change in language-model loss.

conditions.value: all activating dataset examples over 10 million tokens

rows.measure: Share of total loss increase from feature ablation attributable to examples where board was the correct next token
rows.note: The result ties the feature’s causal effect to examples where the induction-predicted token is correct.
rows.check: GELU-2L is a 2-layer model with MLPs, not attention-only, so the V1 link is approximate. Baseline is implicit: no ablation.

source_check.correct: 82% is correct. Retain observed for V4; remove the V1 link. This experiment does not establish V1's attention-only composition mechanism.
source_check.problem: The observed state is unsupported for V1; the tested model and measure do not match that version.

rows.subject: GELU-2L
rows.operation_detail: Measured direct feature attribution by attention head for the board-induction feature.
rows.measure: Fraction of variance in feature activation explained by head 1.6
rows.note: The authors identify head 1.6 as an induction head and report it as the principal contributor to this feature.
rows.check: Same model-kind caveat for V1. The row shows head 1.6 produces the feature; it says nothing about composition with a previous-token head.

source_check.correct: 94% is correct. Retain observed for V4; remove the V1 link. Attribution identifies the feature-producing head, without testing previous-token-head composition.
source_check.problem: The observed state is unsupported for V1; neither its model restriction nor its composition mechanism is tested.

rows.subject: GELU-2L
rows.operation_detail: Attributed board-induction feature activation to source tokens using direct feature attribution.
rows.measure: Fraction of variance explained by board source tokens
rows.note: The paper says the majority of variance is explained by board source tokens overall; the reported value above 99.9% is for activations above the stated threshold.
rows.check: The 99.9% value is conditional on activation >5. Unthresholded, the paper says only 'majority'. Same V1 model-kind caveat.

source_check.correct: Over 99.9% applies after filtering for feature activation above 5. Retain observed for V4; remove the V1 link.
source_check.problem: Source-token copying supports induction behaviour but cannot establish V1 in this model.

rows.subject: GELU-2L
rows.operation_detail: Applied an induction-behavior heuristic to candidate SAE features and a low-head-attribution control group.

conditions.value: 586 features with at least 0.6 weight-based attribution to head 1.6
random sample of 200 examples per feature

rows.measure: Candidate features passing the induction-behavior heuristic
rows.note: The authors describe the heuristic as a crude proof of concept and note it may have false positives and false negatives.
rows.check: Candidates were selected by attribution to head 1.6. 450/586 is a behavioural pass rate on a heuristic the authors call crude.

source_check.correct: 450/586 is correct. Retain observed for V4; remove the V1 link. The heuristic tests feature-level induction behaviour, not previous-token-head composition.
source_check.problem: The behavioural heuristic cannot establish V1's attention-only composition mechanism.

rows.subject: GELU-2L
rows.operation_detail: Applied the same induction-behavior heuristic to features with low attribution to head 1.6.

conditions.value: 500 features with less than 10% attribution to head 1.6
random sample of 200 examples per feature

rows.measure: Control features passing the induction-behavior heuristic
rows.note: Only 3 of 500 low-attribution control features passed the stated threshold.
rows.check: This is a control row. 'Absent' is the expected control outcome, so it supports the contrast with R4 rather than counting against any version.

source_check.correct: 3/500 is correct. Retain absent as the expected V4 control outcome; remove the V1 link.
source_check.problem: The control state is appropriate for the behavioural contrast, but its V1 link is unsupported.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, head 5.1
rows.operation_detail: Measured the induction score on synthetic repeated-token datasets while varying prefix length.

conditions.value: synthetic induction datasets with random repeated tokens
varied; long-prefix regime is at least 2

rows.measure: Average attention to the token induction would suggest comes next (induction score)
rows.value: increases from less than 0.3 to over 0.7 as prefix length enters the long-prefix regime
rows.note: This is a change with prefix length, not a change over training time.
rows.check: GPT-2 Small is not a small attention-only model, so this row has no V1 link. The measure is the dependence of induction score on prefix length.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, head 5.5
rows.operation_detail: Measured the induction score on synthetic repeated-token datasets while varying prefix length.

conditions.value: synthetic induction datasets with random repeated tokens
varied; short prefixes and long-prefix regime are compared

rows.measure: Average attention to the token induction would suggest comes next (induction score)
rows.value: starts at 0.7 for short prefixes; the score rises as prefix length increases
rows.note: The authors contrast this head’s short-prefix score with head 5.1’s sharp increase for long prefixes.
rows.check: No V1 link (not an attention-only model). The value 'rises' is read from Figure 4a, not stated numerically except the 0.7 start.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, head 5.1
rows.operation_detail: Corrupted real long-prefix induction examples by replacing the second repeated prefix token with a random token, leaving one prefix.

conditions.value: long-prefix induction examples from the training distribution
replace the second left repeated token with a different random token

rows.note: The paper describes the intervention as effectively causing head 5.1 to stop doing induction on these examples.
rows.check: No V1 link. The row shows head 5.1 is long-prefix specialised; its induction drops when only one prefix token matches.

source_check.correct: Average induction score falls from 0.55 to 0.05. State: absent under the corrupted one-prefix condition; the authors describe induction as effectively stopping.
source_check.problem: Observed misstates induction behaviour after corruption; the intervention nearly eliminates it.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, head 5.5
rows.operation_detail: Measured the induction score after the same corruption of real long-prefix induction examples.

conditions.value: long-prefix induction examples from the training distribution
replace the second left repeated token with a different random token

rows.note: The paper states that head 5.5 maintains an induction attention pattern under this corruption.
rows.check: No V1 link. The clean baseline for head 5.5 is not stated in the text; it can only be read from Figure 4b.

relationships.condition: GELU-2L layer-1 head 1.6 (2-layer, with MLPs), board-induction feature and 586-feature family
relationships.reason: Head 1.6 explains 94% of the feature's variance. It copies earlier 'board' source tokens (>99.9% at threshold 5), and ablation loss falls mainly on board-next examples. Induction features pass the behaviour heuristic far above control (450/586 vs 3/500). Composition with a previous-token head is untested (R1-R5).
relationships.display_finding: Head 1.6 explained 94% of the board feature's variance and copied earlier 'board' tokens in over 99.9% of cases at threshold 5, with ablation loss concentrated on examples where 'board' came next; the induction heuristic identified 450/586 features versus 3/500 controls, while previous-token composition remained untested.

relationships.display_finding: Both model families contain heads with high induction scores on repeated random tokens and real data.

relation.reason: The study directly measures induction behaviour in trained models and experimentally tests prefix dependence.

tranche.reason: SAE attribution, behavioural heuristics and prefix-corruption experiments provide a different method for testing induction behaviour and head specialization.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. R7's increasing score is stated explicitly in Section 4.2, not merely inferred from the figure; these results do not test training-time emergence or previous-token-head composition.

statements.correction: This paper: head 1.6 explains 94% of board-feature variance; 450/586 candidate features pass the induction heuristic versus 3/500 controls; previous-token-head composition untested; model outside V1's attention-only restriction.
statements.problem: The overlapping results cited through R2, R4 and R5 are correct, but this paper does not establish composition. The L0H2 patching and 98.44% ablation claims are explicitly attributed to the separate lw source and cannot be verified from this paper.

statements.correction: Head 5.1: induction score increases from below 0.3 to above 0.7 with prefix length. GELU-2L: 450/586 candidates versus 3/500 low-attribution controls. Header flags one shared original-source author; Neel Nanda appears among this paper's authors and reference [54]'s authors.
statements.problem: The numerical results are correct. The claim that no header flags author overlap contradicts this study's check-pack header. The control features have low head attribution; matching is not reported.

reader_labels.reason: The feature ablation, source attribution, induction heuristic, and head induction scores support induction-related copying behavior in these tested settings (R1-R4, R6-R9).
